description: One trade finishes and another begins, and the interface conditions, unfinished items, protection requirements, and assumptions must be captured clearly so work is not restarted or damaged.

user_profile.persona: 41-year-old field coordinator specializing in trade-to-trade handoffs
user_profile.context: Past problems came less from bad work than from incomplete handoff information between crews
user_profile.communication_style: Interface-focused and practical, wants responsibility boundaries recorded explicitly

fact_sheet.fact: The project is named the 'Skyview Towers, North Tower' project.
The project site address is 123 Builder's Lane, Metro City, MC 45678.
The specific area for this handoff is Level 12, Zone B, covering suites 1210 through 1218.
The outgoing trade contractor is Apex Drywall Inc.
The incoming trade contractor is Stellar Electrical Solutions.
The Apex Drywall foreman responsible for the sign-off is Carlos Ramirez, contactable at 555-0101.
The Stellar Electrical lead electrician accepting the handoff is Jane Chen, contactable at 555-0102.
The formal handoff inspection and sign-off is scheduled for October 26, 2023.
The start time for the handoff inspection meeting is 9:00 AM local time.
The designated meeting point for the handoff is the Level 12 site office trailer, Room A.
The general contractor's field coordinator overseeing the handoff is Marco Vega.
All Type X fire-rated drywall (5/8 inch) has been installed on demising walls per drawing S-5.2, Rev 4.
Level 4 finish has been applied to all walls in suites 1210-1218, except for designated utility closets.
All ceiling grid backer boards are installed and secured.
Sound insulation batts (Model R-19) have been installed in all interior partition walls prior to closing.
A moisture-resistant 'green board' has been installed in all designated bathroom and kitchenette areas.
A 2-foot by 4-foot section of drywall is intentionally left open behind the main electrical panel location in room 1210's utility closet.
Final sanding and touch-up of wall surfaces will occur after electrical rough-in is complete; this is designated as Punch List item P-12B-001.
The ceiling access panel in the corridor C-12B has not been installed and is stored in Room 1211.
Apex Drywall is scheduled to return on November 15, 2023, for final patching and close-out.
The floor slab in Zone B is broom-swept clean as of October 25, 2023, 4:00 PM.
Temporary power is available via two 120V quad boxes located at columns C4 and F4.
All window openings are sealed with 6-mil plastic sheeting.
Ambient temperature in the work area is maintained at 65°F by temporary heating units.
All outlet and switch box locations have been marked on the floor with blue spray paint by Apex Drywall.
Stellar Electrical must use plastic floor runners (Model FR-36) in all finished corridors.
Newly installed metal corner beads must be protected from damage; replacement cost is $45 per 8-foot section.
No tools or materials are to be leaned against finished drywall surfaces.
Any damage to finished surfaces must be reported to Marco Vega via the ProCore platform within 2 hours.
It is assumed that Stellar Electrical will not require any wall penetrations larger than 6 inches in diameter.
Stellar Electrical assumes responsibility for verifying all box locations against electrical drawings E-3.1 and E-3.2 before installation.
The risk of dust contamination for sensitive electrical components is considered low, as major sanding is complete.
The official handoff is documented on Form 'Trade Handoff Checklist T-12', which must be signed by both parties.
All photos documenting the area's condition at handoff are uploaded to the ProCore project folder '2023-10-26_L12B_Drywall-Elec_Handoff'.

user_needs.description: What is the project name and the specific area for this handoff?
Who are the primary contacts for the outgoing drywall contractor and the incoming electrical contractor?
What is the date, time, and location for the handoff inspection meeting?
user_needs.prediction_reason: Intra-group: After identifying the key personnel, the user will naturally want to know the logistical details of when and where to meet them.

user_needs.description: Which drywall installation, finish, and insulation tasks are complete in the handoff area?
Are there any specific drywall items that are intentionally left unfinished?
user_needs.prediction_reason: CROSS-GROUP: After understanding what work is complete, the immediate and most critical follow-up for a field coordinator is to clarify what work is explicitly NOT complete to avoid confusion.

user_needs.description: When is the drywall contractor scheduled to return to complete their pending work?
user_needs.prediction_reason: Intra-group: Once the user knows there are pending items, they will want to know the schedule for their completion.

user_needs.description: What are the current site conditions regarding cleanliness, temporary power, and ambient temperature?
What protection rules must the incoming electrical crew follow to avoid damaging the finished drywall and corner beads?
user_needs.prediction_reason: CROSS-GROUP: After learning about the current state of the site, the coordinator's focus shifts to maintaining that state and preventing damage, making protection requirements the next logical topic.

user_needs.description: What is the required procedure for reporting any damage to the finished surfaces?
user_needs.prediction_reason: Intra-group: Discussing rules for preventing damage naturally leads to the question of what to do if damage occurs despite the precautions.

user_needs.description: What form records the official handoff, and where are the handoff condition photos uploaded?
user_needs.prediction_reason: CROSS-GROUP: After clarifying the critical details of what is finished and what is pending, the coordinator, who values explicit records, will want to know how this information is being formally captured.
